summary.text: Michelle Kang is the Democratic candidate for the Georgia House of Representatives, District 99, in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against incumbent Republican Matt Reeves.
According to Ballotpedia, Kang was born in Incheon, South Korea, earned a graduate degree from the University of Georgia in 2009 and has worked as an organizer.

paragraphs.text: Michelle Kang was born in Incheon, South Korea, and earned a graduate degree from the University of Georgia in 2009.

In a Ballotpedia survey, Kang described herself as a first-generation Korean American immigrant who came to Georgia in 1992 and who had previously worked as an intellectual property paralegal at a large law firm in Seoul.

She said she worked as a cashier at a dry cleaner after arriving in the United States, and that she pursued a Master's degree in Public Administration at the University of Georgia at age 41 and then worked as center manager at the Asian American Resource Center, where she operated a HUD housing program and provided case management.
She said she joined Senator Raphael Warnock's 2022 re-election campaign, organizing rallies and get-out-the-vote events.
Kang defeated Shelly Abraham in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for District 99, 71.5% to 28.5%.

In the survey, she said her key messages include universal childcare built on Georgia's free Pre-K program, lower taxes on families earning $100,000 or less, and higher taxes on the richest 1% of Georgians.
